payload.text: A mass m moves through a medium with drag force F=-bv and initial speed v₀.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Design a feasible measurement that tests the governing relation; identify the independent variable, dependent variable, and one control.

criteria.description: Design measures the object's speed v at successive times t as it decelerates through the medium; independent variable is elapsed time t, dependent variable is measured speed v, and the drag coefficient b (same object, same fluid) must be held constant across trials.
required_evidence: control: drag coefficient b held constant
accepted_variants: Equivalent scientifically correct notation and reasoning earn credit.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain how the constant time-constant τ=m/b predicted by the linear-drag model, and the assumption that drag stays proportional to v (no turbulence) over the tested speed range, supports your proposed measurement design.

criteria.description: Explain how the constant time-constant τ=m/b predicted by the linear-drag model, and the assumption that drag stays proportional to v (no turbulence) over the tested speed range, supports your proposed measurement design.
required_evidence: time constant τ=m/b is independent of v₀
drag remains linear (proportional to v) over tested range
